transcription.text: Thanks for joining. The goal today is to decide how checkout handles payment retries, because last month's incident double-charged about two hundred customers.
The root cause is that the client retries on a timeout, but the server may have already captured the payment.
We have no idem potency key, so the second attempt looks like a new charge.
My proposal is a server-generated idempotency key stored for twenty-four hours. If the same key arrives again, we return the first result.
I worry about the twenty-four hour window. Bank transfers can settle after two days, so a retry on day three would still double-charge.
Transfers don't go through this path today, so I'd keep it at twenty-four hours for cards and revisit when we add transfers.
Right, and storage cost is not really the constraint here, is it?
It's cheap. Uh, maybe forty... forty gigs a month at current volume.
Let me show how I'd roll it out.
First, turn on the flag in shadow mode, so keys are written but never enforced.
The command is rollout set idempotency, mode shadow, percent five. We start at five percent so a bug in key generation can't touch most traffic.
Now watch the dashboard. The panel you want is would-have-deduped. It should stay near zero except for real client retries.
If that panel jumps above one percent, roll back by setting the mode to off. That's a sign keys are colliding.
Once it's flat for a full day, switch to enforce at five percent, then go to a hundred.
Ramping through twenty-five is optional, I'd only do it before a holiday.
okay lets go with the server side key and twenty four hours for cards thats decided
I still think the window should be configurable per payment method. I don't want to be hard-coding this again.
Let's keep that as an open question until transfers are on the roadmap.
I'll have the shadow rollout up by Friday.
Someone should probably update the client retry docs.
(crosstalk) ...and the changelog too.
